public_text.10:
D. HR4 functions upstream of / positively regulates PAD4 in Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola / Psm-triggered immunity.

In the Arabidopsis EDS1-PAD4-SAG101 SA signalling literature HR4 is recovered as a bona fide PAD4-associated component. Y2H, co-IP and in planta proximity screens place HR4 in the PAD4/EDS1 module and hr4 loss-of-function essentially phenocopies pad4 for Psm-triggered SA accumulation, defence gene expression and resistance. Genetically HR4 is required for normal PAD4 stabilisation/activation and for the full PAD4-dependent transcriptional output on bacterial challenge, i.e. an upstream positive regulatory requirement for the defence modulator PAD4 in the Psm pathosystem. 

That functional regulatory requirement entails the physical association described in E, so E is true in the sense of a binding partner, but the established description in the Psm literature is the regulatory dependence rather than a generic interactor statement. 

The powdery mildew / EHM / actin module is presented as a distinct context for a powdery mildew-associated HR4 activity. A is formally incorrect as written because ADF3 is an actin depolymerising / severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, and the HR4–ADF3 link is not the defining PAD4-context characterisation. B and C describe the EHM-targeted, broad-spectrum powdery mildew resistance framing. In the canonical Arabidopsis PAD4-interacting HR4 that is discussed in the bacterial defence literature the reproducibly demonstrated, functionally defining feature is the requirement for and upstream positive modulation of PAD4-dependent defence on Psm infection.
public_text.2:
C. It is targeted to the Extrahaustorial membrane during infection by the powdery mildew pathogen

The molecular and localisation definition that is most discriminative for the Arabidopsis powdery-mildew HR4 immunity factor is EHM recruitment at the host-pathogen interface. On infection with Golovinomyces/Blumeria spp. HR4 is induced and relocates/stably associates with the plant plasma membrane invagination that surrounds the fungal haustorium, i.e. the extrahaustorial membrane, a localisation that underlies the HR4-mediated powdery-mildew resistance module and its reported actin-cytoskeletal read-out with ADF3.

That makes A inaccurate as written. The actin factor that is co-isolated in the powdery-mildew HR4 module is ADF3, which is an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, so “interactor of the actin assembly factor ADF3” is a mischaracterisation even if an HR4–ADF3 link is invoked.

B is a downstream functional consequence of the EHM-targeted module but is less specific than the localisation claim. 

The PAD4-centred statements D and E describe the EDS1-PAD4-SAG101 SA signalling axis in the Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola / Psm bacterial pathosystem. A physical PAD4 association can be recovered in Y2H/co-IP/proximity screens, which is the basis for E, and the genetic epistasis in Psm is often framed as an upstream regulatory requirement, which is the basis for D. Those bacterial PAD4 signalling read-outs are presented in the literature as a distinct context from the EHM-targeted, powdery-mildew-associated HR4 resistance factor defined by haustorial membrane recruitment. The least contestable, locally specific characterisation of the powdery-mildew HR4 factor remains EHM targeting during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection.

Powdery mildew/EHM/actin camp – C with B/A nuance
* Colleague2 remains the clearest C defender, with the EHM targeting described as the discriminative localisation feature for the powdery mildew-associated HR4 factor: induced and stably associated with the extrahaustorial membrane surrounding haustoria during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection, underlying actin-linked resistance. B is seen as a downstream consequence of the EHM module, less specific than localisation. The PAD4-centred statements are presented as a distinct bacterial context, separate from the EHM-targeted powdery mildew module.

* ADF3 mischaracterisation persists in option A and is corrected across colleagues.
* Context conflict unresolved: PAD4 bacterial SA signalling vs powdery mildew EHM/actin localisation. Several colleagues explicitly separate the two as distinct functional/localisation contexts for HR4, suggesting possible conflation of literature or context-dependent activity.

PAD4/Psm module. Physical PAD4 association is repeatedly cited: Y2H, co-IP, in planta proximity recover HR4 in the EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1 SA module. Genetic epistasis in Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola / Psm is described as hr4 loss-of-function phenocopying pad4 for SA accumulation, defence gene expression and resistance, with HR4 required for PAD4 stabilisation/activation. Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 maintain D as best description: HR4 functions upstream/positively regulates PAD4 in Psm-triggered immunity; the requirement is the experimentally established functional read-out, and E is said to understate the demonstrated regulatory dependency. Colleagues 11,3,4,6,8,9 now argue for the conservative E: HR4 is a bona fide PAD4 interactor recovered in screens and placed in the EDS1-PAD4-SAG101 network; D is a functional superset/inference from that physical association. Colleague 11 explicitly frames D as superset and E as minimally overstated, repeatedly reproduced feature.

Powdery mildew/EHM/actin module. Colleague 2 alone now holds C in round 2: HR4 is recruited to/stably associates with the extrahaustorial membrane at the haustorial interface during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection, the discriminative localisation feature of powdery mildew resistance. B is treated as downstream consequence of EHM targeting and less specific. ADF3 wording error persists: ADF3 is an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, so option A is inaccurate in wording and is disputed as a canonical HR4 interactor. The HR4-ADF3 actin-remodelling claim is presented by the powdery mildew camp as mechanistic basis for broad-spectrum powdery mildew resistance.

Changes/positions round 2. Colleague 10 flipped E→D, Colleague 11 flipped C→E back, Colleague 2 flipped E→C, Colleague 8 flipped C→E, Colleague 9 flipped C→E, Colleague 3 flipped C→E. Vote round 2: E=6, D=5, C=1. A remains weak, B compatible with C but non-discriminative.

Unresolved. The PAD4 interaction/regulation remains the most replicated core molecular definition I know, with E being the most conservative, experimentally secure biochemical statement and D capturing the functional upstream relationship repeatedly described for Psm. The powdery mildew EHM/ADF3/broad-spectrum resistance claims remain strongly asserted by a persistent minority and raise the question of whether the literature conflates two different functional annotations under the same HR4 name or whether HR4 genuinely has dual roles. Terminology issue on ADF3 persists and the primary characterisation of HR4 is still contested between physical interactor status and upstream regulatory requirement in Psm versus EHM localisation in powdery mildew.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains centred on two competing contextualisations of HR4 – an EDS1-PAD4-SAG101 SA bacterial defence module and a powdery-mildew / extrahaustorial membrane / actin module – with gene/context identity still unresolved.

PAD4 / Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola / Psm branch
* Physical interaction evidence is repeatedly cited: HR4 recovered as a bona fide PAD4 binding partner in Y2H, co-IP and in planta proximity screens and co-purifies with the EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1 module. Colleagues 11,3,4,6,8,9 now hold this as the most reproducibly demonstrated, minimally overstated molecular feature.
* Functional read-out in Psm: hr4 loss-of-function essentially phenocopies pad4 for SA accumulation, PAD4-dependent defence gene expression and resistance; HR4 is reported required for normal PAD4 stabilisation/activation. Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 frame this as an upstream positive regulatory requirement and support D: HR4 regulates the defence modulator PAD4 in Psm defence.
* Tension D vs E persists within this camp. D supporters argue the epistasis and requirement make ‘regulates’ the established functional description; E supporters argue D is a functional superset/interpretation of the secure biochemical association and that ‘one of the interactors’ is the conservative, repeatedly reproduced statement. Colleague10 now moves C→D, stating the regulatory requirement entails the physical association but the literature description is regulatory.

Powdery mildew / EHM / actin branch
* C supporters 2, previously 11,3,8,9, continue to define HR4 by EHM targeting during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection: induced/recruited to and stably associated with the extrahaustorial membrane surrounding the haustorium, underpinning powdery mildew resistance.
* B, broad-spectrum powdery mildew defence contribution, is asserted as downstream of EHM targeting by the EHM bloc but denied as defining by the PAD4 bloc.
* ADF3 naming error remains corrected repeatedly: the co-isolated factor is ADF3, an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, so option A is inaccurate in wording. Colleague2 now moves A→C and notes the mischaracterisation.

Cross-cutting / shifts
* Several colleagues moved away from the EHM narrative in this round: 3,8,9 moved C→E; 10 moved C→D. Only Colleague2 still holds C as the discriminative localisation definition, arguing the PAD4 statements describe a distinct bacterial context from the EHM-targeted powdery-mildew HR4 factor.
* Colleague11,4,6,8,9 now treat PAD4-interacting HR4 and EHM-targeted powdery mildew HR4 as functionally distinct / context-conflicted annotations; Colleague2,3,9 earlier treated EHM targeting as primary for the same protein.
* No consensus on whether the question intends the PAD4/SA bacterial definition or the powdery-mildew/EHM definition.

State of belief: Both modules remain live. The PAD4 physical interactor status E is the most replicated biochemical claim with independent screens; the upstream regulatory description D is the functional interpretation of that interaction in Psm assays and is strongly supported by genetic epistasis. EHM targeting C is consistently described for the powdery-mildew-associated HR4 literature but support has narrowed. I am leaning toward E as the most conservative, repeatedly demonstrated feature across the PAD4/EDS1 literature, while recognising D as the functional superset that many colleagues prefer and the EHM context as the remaining alternative if the question refers to the powdery-mildew annotation. Disambiguation of gene identity/context is still unresolved.

reflection_text.2:
The deliberation remains unresolved but the distribution has shifted toward the PAD4/Psm axis, with D and E competing and the powdery mildew/EHM camp now a minority.

PAD4/Psm regulatory camp – D
* Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 hold that in the Arabidopsis EDS1-PAD4-SAG101 SA literature HR4’s functionally defining feature in Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola / Psm triggered immunity is an upstream positive requirement for PAD4.
Evidence cited: hr4 loss-of-function phenocopies pad4 for SA accumulation, PAD4-dependent defence gene expression and resistance; HR4 required for PAD4 stabilisation/activation; genetic epistasis places HR4 upstream of PAD4-mediated outputs. Colleague10 moved C→D this round; Colleague1 and 12 argue E is technically true but understates the demonstrated regulatory dependency. The physical association is accepted as real but described as the mechanistic basis for the regulatory phenotype.

PAD4 physical interaction camp – E
* Colleagues 11,3,4,6,8,9 now defend E as the minimally overstated, most reproducibly demonstrated molecular fact.
Evidence cited: Y2H, co-IP and in planta proximity screens repeatedly recover HR4 as a bona fide PAD4 binding partner in the EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1 module; co-purification with PAD4/EDS1 in planta. D is framed as the functional read-out / superset of that interaction. Colleagues 3,8,9 moved C→E this round, reinforcing the view that the secure biochemical statement is the interactor status. Colleague11 maintains the physical association is the basis for the reported Psm requirement.

Powdery mildew/EHM/actin camp – C with B/A nuance
* Colleague2 remains the clearest C defender, with the EHM targeting described as the discriminative localisation feature for the powdery mildew-associated HR4 factor: induced and stably associated with the extrahaustorial membrane surrounding haustoria during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection, underlying actin-linked resistance. A is repeatedly corrected: ADF3 is an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, so “interactor of the actin assembly factor ADF3” is a wording error. B is seen as a downstream consequence of the EHM module, less specific than localisation. The PAD4-centred statements are presented as a distinct bacterial context, separate from the EHM-targeted powdery mildew module.

Points of tension preserved
* ADF3 mischaracterisation persists in option A and is corrected across colleagues.
* Context conflict unresolved: PAD4 bacterial SA signalling vs powdery mildew EHM/actin localisation. Several colleagues explicitly separate the two as distinct functional/localisation contexts for HR4, suggesting possible conflation of literature or context-dependent activity.
* D vs E nuance remains central: D asserts regulatory upstream control of PAD4 in Psm; E asserts physical interaction only. Multiple shifts this round C→E and C→D indicate instability, with some colleagues now accepting both as true but preferring the more conservative biochemical statement E, others preferring the functional description D.
* B “broad spectrum powdery mildew defence” is asserted as outcome of the EHM module but disputed as primary characterisation by PAD4 camp.

Current working understanding: There is strong replicated biochemical evidence for HR4 as a PAD4-interacting component of EDS1-PAD4-SAG101 SA immunity with genetic evidence for functional requirement upstream of PAD4 in Psm. A minority maintains HR4’s defining feature is EHM targeting during powdery mildew infection with actin-linked activity. The ADF3 wording error is settled. No consensus on which definition is primary for the question; the three viable candidates are D, E and C, with D and E now the main contenders, E currently holding a slight numerical edge 6 vs 5, C isolated. The regulatory vs interactor framing and the bacterial vs powdery mildew context conflict remain unresolved.
reflection_text.3:
The discussion remains split three ways, with a PAD4/Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola bacterial defence cluster, a powdery mildew/extrahaustorial membrane/actin cluster, and continued uncertainty over whether the PAD4-interacting HR4 and the EHM-targeted powdery mildew HR4 refer to the same Arabidopsis protein or to a conflation of contexts.

PAD4-centric evidence that keeps recurring in round 2:
* HR4 is reproducibly recovered as a bona fide PAD4 binding partner in Y2H, co-IP and in planta proximity screens and is placed in the EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1-SA module.
* In Psm-inoculated Arabidopsis hr4 loss-of-function phenocopies pad4 for SA accumulation, PAD4-dependent defence gene expression and resistance; HR4 is required for normal stabilisation/activation of PAD4-dependent signalling.
* D supporters 1,10,12,5,7 frame this as a functional upstream positive regulatory requirement: HR4 regulates the defence modulator PAD4 in Psm defence, arguing the regulatory wording captures the epistasis and requirement better than a generic binding label.
* E supporters 11,3,4,6,8,9 accept the physical association and the genetic requirement but argue the minimally overstated, directly demonstrated feature is the bona fide PAD4 interactor status in E, with D being the functional superset/interpretation of that interaction. Colleague 10 now moves to D, noting E is true as binding but the Psm literature’s established description is regulatory.

Powdery mildew/EHM/actin evidence that keeps recurring:
* During Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection HR4 is induced and relocalises to/stably associates with the host plasma membrane invagination around the haustorium, i.e. the extrahaustorial membrane at the host–pathogen interface. Colleague 2 now explicitly defends C as the most discriminative localisation feature for the powdery mildew HR4 factor.
* The HR4–ADF3 module is invoked for actin remodelling in powdery mildew resistance. The correction is now unanimous: ADF3 is an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, so option A is inaccurate in wording even if an HR4–ADF3 link is discussed.
* B “contributes to defence against the broad spectrum of powdery mildew pathogens” is compatible with the EHM module but is less specific than C.

Belief dynamics update after round 2:
* Colleague 10 moved D from E, Colleague 2 holds C, Colleague 11 stays E, Colleague 3 moved to E, Colleague 4 stays E, Colleague 6 stays E, Colleague 8 moved to E, Colleague 9 stays E.
* Current counts: D ≈1,10,12,5,7; E ≈11,3,4,6,8,9; C ≈2.
* E is now the numerically largest bloc, D the second largest, C a minority. The PAD4 interaction E is the most stable conservative claim; D is the strongest functional claim in the Psm pathosystem.

Unresolved questions persisting:
* Identity/context conflation: do the PAD4-interacting bacterial-defence HR4 and the EHM-targeted powdery mildew HR4 describe the same Arabidopsis gene or two different functional annotations that share the name? Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 treat them as distinct contexts with the bacterial PAD4 axis being primary; colleagues 2 defends EHM targeting as the defining feature.
* Relative primacy: is the defining experimental feature physical PAD4 association, the upstream regulatory requirement for PAD4 in Psm, or EHM recruitment during powdery mildew infection?
* Wording accuracy: A remains weakened by the ADF3 assembly-factor mislabel.

Current working synthesis: Physical PAD4 association is experimentally the most replicated molecular feature and underpins the reported upstream regulatory requirement of HR4 for PAD4-dependent outputs in Psm. The regulatory formulation D is a valid functional interpretation supported by genetic epistasis and phenocopy, but E remains the minimally overstated biochemical statement. EHM targeting during powdery mildew infection is repeatedly cited with localisation data but its relationship to the PAD4-interacting HR4 remains contested and is argued by a minority as a distinct/primary characterisation.

Colleagues 1,10,12,5,7 frame this as an upstream positive regulatory requirement and support D: HR4 regulates the defence modulator PAD4 in Psm defence.
* Tension D vs E persists within this camp. D supporters argue the epistasis and requirement make ‘regulates’ the established functional description; E supporters argue D is a functional superset/interpretation of the secure biochemical association and that ‘one of the interactors’ is the conservative, repeatedly reproduced statement. Colleague10 now moves C→D, stating the regulatory requirement entails the physical association but the literature description is regulatory.

Powdery mildew / EHM / actin branch
* C supporters 2, previously 11,3,8,9, continue to define HR4 by EHM targeting during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection: induced/recruited to and stably associated with the extrahaustorial membrane surrounding the haustorium, underpinning powdery mildew resistance.

* ADF3 naming error remains corrected repeatedly: the co-isolated factor is ADF3, an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, so option A is inaccurate in wording. Colleague2 now moves A→C and notes the mischaracterisation.

Cross-cutting / shifts
* Several colleagues moved away from the EHM narrative in this round: 3,8,9 moved C→E; 10 moved C→D. Only Colleague2 still holds C as the discriminative localisation definition, arguing the PAD4 statements describe a distinct bacterial context from the EHM-targeted powdery-mildew HR4 factor.

* No consensus on whether the question intends the PAD4/SA bacterial definition or the powdery-mildew/EHM definition.

State of belief: Both modules remain live. 1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: D. HR4 functions upstream of PAD4 and is required for PAD4-dependent defense output in Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola / Psm infection.

The physical HR4-PAD4 association that Colleagues 11, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9 cite is real and reproducible. Y2H, co-IP and in planta proximity do recover HR4 in the EDS1-PAD4-SAG101 module and HR4 co-purifies with the PAD4 network. That biochemical placement is the mechanistic basis for the phenotype.

In the Psm system the phenotype that is repeatedly tested is regulatory and directional. hr4 loss-of-function essentially phenocopies pad4 for SA accumulation, PAD4-dependent defence gene expression and resistance to Psm, and HR4 is needed for normal PAD4 stabilisation/activation during bacterial challenge. The genetic epistasis places HR4 upstream of the PAD4-mediated transcriptional program, which is how the Psm literature frames the relationship: HR4 acts as a positive regulator required for full PAD4 signalling, not simply as a passive binding partner in the interactome.

Saying HR4 is “one of the interactors of PAD4” as in E is technically true for the screens, but it understates the established functional description and collapses a demonstrated requirement into a generic binding statement. The regulatory formulation in D captures the requirement that has been repeatedly tested genetically and biochemically in the Psm pathosystem and is the functionally specific description of HR4 in that defence context.

The EHM targeting / ADF3 actin-remodelling narrative in C and the ADF3 wording in A describe a powdery mildew-associated localisation module. ADF3 is an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, and that powdery mildew EHM/ADF3 context is presented in the literature as distinct from the classic PAD4-EDS1 SA axis where the HR4 requirement for PAD4-mediated immunity is most cleanly demonstrated. For the canonical Arabidopsis PAD4-interacting HR4 characterised in Psm defence the secure, functionally accurate statement is the upstream regulatory role for PAD4.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains anchored on the Arabidopsis EDS1-PAD4-SAG101 bacterial SA axis versus the powdery mildew/EHM/actin narrative, with persistent uncertainty about identity/context conflation of HR4.

PAD4/Psm cluster evidence repeatedly cited in round 4:
* HR4 is reproducibly recovered as a bona fide PAD4 binding partner in Y2H, co-IP and in planta proximity, co-purifying with EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1.
* In Psm-inoculated Arabidopsis hr4 loss-of-function phenocopies pad4 for SA accumulation, PAD4-dependent defence gene expression and resistance; HR4 is required for normal stabilisation/activation of PAD4-dependent signalling.
* D supporters 1,12,5,7 argue the functionally tested description is an upstream positive regulatory requirement for PAD4 in Psm defence, with E being true but understating the demonstrated dependency.
* E supporters 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 accept the physical association and the genetic requirement but argue the minimally overstated, directly demonstrated feature is the bona fide PAD4 interactor status in E, with D being the functional superset/interpretation.

Belief dynamics after round 4:
* Colleague 2 moved D → E this round.
* Current public positions: E = 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 (8), D = 1,12,5,7 (4), C = 0.
* E is now the clear numerical majority; D is the second bloc. No support remains for C.

Powdery mildew/EHM/actin cluster:
* EHM targeting during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection and HR4-ADF3 actin remodelling are still invoked by minority historical positions.
* Correction remains unanimous: ADF3 is an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, so option A is inaccurate in wording even if an HR4–ADF3 link is discussed.
* B “contributes to defence against broad spectrum powdery mildew pathogens” is compatible with the EHM module but less specific than C and unsupported in current voting.

Unresolved questions persisting:
* Identity/context conflation: do the PAD4-interacting bacterial-defence HR4 and the EHM-targeted powdery mildew HR4 describe the same Arabidopsis protein or conflated annotations?
* Relative primacy: is the defining experimental feature physical PAD4 association, the upstream regulatory requirement for PAD4 in Psm, or EHM recruitment during powdery mildew?
* Wording accuracy: A remains weakened by ADF3 assembly-factor mislabel.

Current working synthesis: Physical PAD4 association is experimentally the most replicated molecular feature and underpins the reported upstream regulatory requirement of HR4 for PAD4-dependent outputs in Psm. The regulatory formulation D is a valid functional interpretation supported by genetic epistasis and phenocopy, but E remains the minimally overstated biochemical statement most consistently reproduced across screens and is now the majority position. EHM targeting during powdery mildew infection is repeatedly cited with localisation data but is defended by no one in round 4 and is argued by the majority as a distinct/context-conflicted characterisation.

Current round 4 positions: E is held by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 =8. D is held by Colleagues 1,12,5,7 =4. No colleague now defends C, B or A. Colleague 2 has flipped back from D in the previous round to E, reinforcing the E camp. Colleagues 1,12,5,7 remain consistent D defenders.

Replicated biochemical evidence continues to be the core anchor cited by both camps: Y2H, co-IP and in planta proximity screens recover HR4 as a bona fide PAD4 binding partner; HR4 co-purifies with the EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1 module in planta. That physical placement is taken as the experimental basis for the Psm phenotype.

Functional genetic evidence for the bacterial context is consistently reiterated: hr4 loss-of-function essentially phenocopies pad4 for SA accumulation, PAD4-dependent defence gene expression and resistance to Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola / Psm; HR4 is required for normal PAD4 stabilisation/activation during bacterial challenge; genetic epistasis places HR4 upstream of the PAD4-mediated transcriptional programme.

The D vs E nuance is now the central disagreement. The D camp - Colleagues 1,12,5,7 - argues the Psm phenotype is regulatory and directional, that HR4 acts as a positive upstream regulator required for full PAD4 signalling, and that “interactor” understates the demonstrated requirement. The E camp - Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 - argues E is the minimally overstated, repeatedly reproduced molecular fact and that D is the functional read-out / superset interpretation of that interaction. B and C describing broad-spectrum powdery mildew defence and EHM targeting during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection are now presented as a distinct powdery mildew/EHM/actin-remodelling narrative that is context-conflicted with the canonical PAD4-EDS1 SA axis. reflection_text.9:
The discussion remains split between a functional regulatory claim for Psm/PAD4 and a minimal biochemical claim for PAD4 interaction, with the minimal biochemical claim now numerically dominant, while the powdery-mildew/EHM bloc has no public proponent in round 4.

PAD4/Psm functional regulatory bloc – D:
* Colleagues 1,12,5,7 hold D. They accept the HR4-PAD4 physical association as real – Y2H, co-IP, in planta proximity recover HR4 in EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1 and HR4 co-purifies with the module – but stress the repeatedly tested phenotype in Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola/Psm is regulatory and directional. hr4 loss-of-function essentially phenocopies pad4 for SA accumulation, PAD4-dependent defence gene expression and Psm resistance; HR4 is required for normal PAD4 stabilisation/activation. Genetic epistasis places HR4 upstream of the PAD4-mediated transcriptional programme. D is therefore presented as the experimentally established functional read-out; E is described as technically true but a deliberate understatement that collapses a demonstrated upstream dependency into generic binding.

PAD4 physical-interactor minimal bloc – E:
* Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 hold E. The most reproducibly demonstrated molecular feature for the canonical Arabidopsis SA/EDS1-PAD4 HR4 protein is a bona fide physical association with PAD4. Recovery in Y2H/co-IP/proximity and co-purification with EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1 is consistently reported and is the experimental basis for the Psm phenotype described above. D “HR4 regulates the defence modulator PAD4 in plant defence against the Psm” is the functional read-out / superset/interpretation of that interaction; if D is accepted E is logically entailed. E is the minimally overstated, directly demonstrated statement that underlies the upstream regulatory effect described in D.

Powdery mildew/EHM/ADF3 bloc:
* No colleague endorses C in round 4. A is repeatedly corrected: the actin factor co-isolated in the powdery-mildew associated module is ADF3, an actin depolymerising/severing factor, not an actin assembly factor, so “interactor of the actin assembly factor ADF3” is false as worded. B broad-spectrum powdery mildew defence and C EHM targeting during Golovinomyces/Blumeria infection are treated as a distinct localisation/functional context – EHM recruitment and HR4–ADF3 actin remodelling – presented in the literature as context-conflicted with the canonical PAD4-interacting HR4 bacterial SA axis. Colleague 4 notes no proponent for C remains after round 3.

Evidence repeatedly cited:
* Physical: HR4 recovered as PAD4 binding partner in Y2H, co-IP, in planta proximity; co-purifies with EDS1-PAD4-SAG101/ADR1.
* Genetic/functional in Psm: hr4 loss phenocopies pad4 for SA, defence gene expression, resistance; HR4 needed for PAD4 stabilisation/activation; upstream positive regulation.

Errors/corrections stable:
* ADF3 mislabelled as assembly factor in A.
* D and E overlap: E is physical interaction, D is functional/regulatory interpretation in Psm.

Changes / volatility:
* Round 3: 10 D→E; 2 C→D. Round 4: 2 moves back E ← D, so 2 is now with the E bloc. D bloc remains 1,12,5,7; E bloc is 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 – 8 vs 4.
* C has lost all public support in this round.

Unresolved:
* Whether a single HR4 gene underlies both the PAD4 bacterial SA signalling module and the powdery-mildew EHM/ADF3 actin-remodelling module, or whether this reflects a naming/context collision between two functionally distinct descriptions. On replicated biochemical grounds E is the least contestable molecular definition for the canonical PAD4-interacting HR4, with D as its functional consequence in Psm-triggered immunity.
